question.text: In the presence of peroxide, $\mathrm{HCl}$ and $\mathrm{HI}$ do not give anti-Markownikoff's addition of alkenes because:

options.text: One of the steps is endothermic in $\mathrm{HCl}$ and $\mathrm{HI}$
$\mathrm{HCl}$ is oxidizing and the $\mathrm{HI}$ is reducing
All the steps are exothermic is $\mathrm{HCl}$ and $\mathrm{HI}$

solution.text: Anti-Markownikoff addition is possible only in case of $\mathrm{HBr}$ and not in $\mathrm{HCl}$ and $\mathrm{HI}$. In $\mathrm{HBr}$ both the chain initiation and propagation steps are exothermic, while in $\mathrm{HCl}$, first step is exothermic, and second step is endothermic and in HI, no step is exothermic. Hence $\mathrm{HCl}$ and $\mathrm{HI}$ do not undergo anti-Markownikoff's addition.
